A week in November (State Capture)

By: Joy Summers | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Another big week in South Africa as the NPA steps down on its charges against the finance minister, and the courts deal a blow to the President

Summary:
A week in November
By Tuesday evening it already felt like Friday. The wave that has been building over South Africa’s political landscape, this week became a Tsunami. No one is quite sure where it will end. Will the president who has defied the odds, public sentiment and even calls from within his own party to resign, listen? It seems unlikely, but sentiment may be changing deep within the ANC’s core at the NEC. Who knows what the end of the week may look like.








Further information:
The stakes are high but on Monday and Tuesday, the President and his men who seem hell bent on looting the Treasury and destroying anyone in their path, became substantially weaker. On Wednesday the people – business, labour, civil society, religious groups and political parties came out on the streets to make their voices heard. The SAVE South Africa campaign added impetus to a process that is already under way in the courts.

Lawfare was once again the order of the day – On Monday the NPA head Shaun Abrahams announced at an impromptu press conference that he was dropping the charges against finance minister Pravin Gordhan. There had never been a case and Abrahams knew it. The case instigated by SARS boss Tom Moyane had descended into a bizarre episode in a SARS boardroom a week before when it became clear that the NPA was still looking for evidence way after they had made such a public announcement on the finance minister and two SARS commissioners. The Vlock Symington hostage drama in the SARS boardroom was up there with some of the best SA could offer – funny if it wasn’t for the fact that the nations fortunes hinge on what happens next.

The calls for Abrahams head came thick and fast. He was called Shaun the sheep, internet memes with egg on his face did the rounds and the Law Society called for his resignation.
But Abrahams was having none of it – was he embarrassed – he preferred not to answer the question. Would he resign? certainly not. That his decision had cost the country 50 billion rand and an almost certain downgrade seemed lost on him.

Banana Republic we are not said the Business Day – more like an absurd soap opera – with each episode getting more and more bizarre.

And that was only Monday. Tuesday was the scene of yet another day of high drama as Des Van Rooyen- the weekend finance minister decided to bring an urgent application to court to stop the release of the public protectors report. That application was accompanied by a second from most of the opposition parties who won the right to be joined as parties in the decision on whether or not the public protectors report on State Capture should be released.

If there was any doubt about the new PP approach. Well she had none. To quote Phillip De Wet- niks. Nader. None – She would go whichever way the court decided. Not much fight here

By Tuesday evening, a full bench of the high court dismissed Van Rooyens urgent application with costs. A glimmer of light and hope for SA future shone from a high court window.

On Wednesday the only real decision will be whether or not the court releases the report or not. The report is final. The president is weaker. Thursday and Friday may yet prove more interesting than we can possibly imagine.

Press Release:


State Capture Report
Following a week of intense political drama, the Public Protector’s long-awaited State Capture Report has finally been released and it’s damning about the president and his relationship with the Gupta family. Will the tangled web finally close in on Zuma and those implicated?


Script:


STATE OF CAPTURE FINAL SCRIPT

Commentary One
This week South Africa’s unsettling narrative unfolded in a dramatic day in the capital City

Up sound EFF man
Two families. Just two have families have shattered this country!

Commentary two
Gupta’s and Zuma’s. Money and Power, a secret report and a determined protector of the public. Our blockbuster lurched from one incredible scene to the next.

Kriegler
We have had an exciting week!

Commentary Three
Chairperson of freedom under law, retired Justice Johann Kriegler

Kriegler
Really the lawyers have given the public an exciting week. It’s not over, Mr Abrahams is in parliament …and that is good, it shows our democracy is alive and well

Commentary Four
Save South Africa, a campaign against state capture, brought together powerful voices at a people’s assembly in downtown Pretoria

Justice Zak Yacoob. Former justice Constitutional court
Our Constitution imposes upon us a duty to get rid of JZ, to clean up our political parties and to ensure in the long term that we create a society which the vision our constitution demands

Commentary Five
So early Monday morning, the finance minister was facing trumped up fraud charges, the outgoing public protectors report was under lock and key, and the President was about to spend thousands on lawyers to ensure it stayed there

LINK SARS
This is a story with many chapters and sub plots, but at least some of it begins here in this building behind me.

Commentary Six
When the Gupta’s landed at Waterkloof, Tom Moyane was sent to investigate. Now he is commissioner of SARS, the presidents ally, and no friend of his boss finance minister Pravin Gordhan.



Adrian Lackay Former spokesperson SARS
There was a clear breakdown of a working relationship in trust between the minister and the SARS commissioner

Commentary seven
Adrian Lackay is a casualty of a bigger war waged to capture SARS. He has just co-authored this book to prove that stories about a so called rogue unit were not only false but deliberately spread to hollow out SARS investigators and weaken the institution. SARS rejects the allegation

Adrian
When 2015 came it was more than apparent to me that TOM MOYANE was never going to do anything to dispel the rogue unit story- they were not going to protect the institution

Commentary eight
Unable to do his job honestly, he left, and is now being sued by Moyane for defamation, for a letter he wrote to parliament about SARS

Adrian
As Max Du Plessis argued in court on Tuesday is that the SARS commissioner is abusing the laws by continuing to muzzle people and prevent them from speaking out.

Commentary nine
The Hawks meanwhile seem intent on finding anything to destroy Pravin Gordhan, and the NPA thought they had found it, when national director, Shaun Abrahams announced to a shocked nation they were charging Gordhan and two former commissioners with fraud.

Shaun Abrahams
The days of disrespecting the NPA are over, the days of non accountability of senior officials are over. I hope that answers your question. Next question please

Commentary ten
But his decision backfired. Thousands of South Africans believed the charges were an attempt by the President to remove Gordhan, and rallied to support him. Political editor Karima Brown

Karima Brown
I think it’s a seminal week, there has been a tectonic shift in the politics of SA It changed when Abrahams charged Gordhan and signaled the end of the grip that Zuma has in the ANC and on the state

Commentary eleven
Wednesday 2nd November, Gordhan was scheduled to appear in court. Then this happened

Up sound Vlok Symington
excuse me I am being kept against my will

The Hawks held SARS deputy director Vlok Symington in a boardroom. They were still scrambling for evidence AFTER the finance minister had been charged!

Up Sound Vlok Symington
Talk to me. Why can I not open the door?

Commentary twelve
Then journalists placed Shaun Abrahams at Luthuli house, meeting the President the day before he charged Pravin

Abrahams
I can assure you there has been no political interference in this matter

Bongani
Is this about incompetence or is it about decisions made for political considerations?

Justice Johann Kriegler
I had thought for a long time perhaps over generously that it could just be incompetence but I have come to the conclusion it was malicious intent

Commentary Thirteen
So Monday this past week was probably not his finest, as Abrahams did his best to spin an embarrassing about turn and withdrew the charges

Abrahams
As such I have directed the summons to be withdrawn with immediate effect

Commentary
Policy and political analyst Professor Tinyiko Maluleke

Tinyiko Maluleke
Shaun Abrahams should have known that there was no case against Pravin from the beginning. So either he is playing the fool or he doesn’t know. If he doesn’t know its horrifying there is someone like that occupies a position like this

Commentary fourteen
All week, even in parliament, Abrahams was asked the same question. Why should he keep his job? But Abrahams has dug in for the long haul

Up Sound Abrahams
Will I resign? Certainly not! Certainly not!

LINK
By Monday evening the rand had rallied a little, the finance minister was safe and by implication so was the treasury- at least for now. Ahead lay Tuesday – state capture day.



01st November NORTH GAUTENG HIGH COURT
EFF Advocate Up Sound
What is clear is that there is a desperate attempt to try and prohibit the publication of this report

Commentary fifteen
The opposition parties, and Vytjie Mentor were determined to fight the suppression of the Public protector’s report by the President and minister Des Van Rooyen.

Dunstan Mlambo
We would like to take time to consider those applications

Gauteng Judge President Dunstan Mlambo led a full bench of the high court

Bongani
What is the cost of all of this?
Justice Kriegler
Oh! I would think several million rand only on the state capture case, let alone the Abrahams cases and the Ipid case and yet its not over …

Bongani
Judge do you support the idea that if people in government bring what may turn out to be frivolous cases then they should pay for the costs in their personal capacity
Kriegler
Oh yes my support is not all that important, that is the law!

LINK
Everybody knows a lawyer joke right? yet it was the lawyers that held the line even as the
Nelson Mandela foundation warned the wheels were coming off the vehicle, that is our state

Commentary sixteen
Tuesday drew to a close. The opposition had convinced the court they could oppose the interdict but the report still remained a secret. On Wednesday anticipation hung over the capital city

Church drums montage. WEDNESDAY 2nd NOVEMBER 2016

Familiar faces dotted the pews in this people’s assembly, titans of the struggle, here to voice their displeasure at the destruction of the democratic project they nurtured

Up sound Itumeleng Mosala
I wish Steve Biko was here I wish Sobukwe was here, I wish Mandela was here

Commentary seventeen
But this wasn’t just a gathering of the political celebrities as Barbara Hogan reminded us

Barbara Hogan
At this very moment Adrian Lackay fighting a R10 million case. There is Johan van Loggerenburg / vlok Symington, Anwa dramat, Shadrack Sibiya ….people who have lived lives of quiet despair because the state has turned on them with all its might for doing the right thing

Commentary eighteen
Marika Muller left SARS disillusioned by what she witnessed

Marika
I couldn’t do my job in an ethical fashion
Bongani
Why is Save SA so important
Marika Muller
Its about keeping the wolf from the door, if SARS goes if it is no longer trusted, if treasury falls there is no one to stop the looting
How close is the wolf to the door?
Marika
Its at the door. Its knocking. Its right there!

Commentary nineteen WED 2nd November
Outside the doors of the high court, the EFF grew impatient. Inside the president’s legal team slugged it out with the advocates for the opposition

But then, an unexpected turn of events as news spread fast across the capital

Barbara Hogan
We have just got word that the president has withdrawn his application

Up sound wild crowd

The people had spoken. The president had buckled

Commentary Twenty
Before sunset on Wednesday, Madonsela’s State of Capture report was released. The President it said, had violated the executive ethics code and refused to answer her questions

LINK
The remedial action ordered in the state capture report is nothing short of inspired because it addresses the president’s constant complaint that he wasn’t given ample opportunity to make representations well now he will have to do so before a commission of enquiry and he won’t be able to select his own judge

Commentary Twenty- one
But can he survive the damning observations in the report?

Karima Brown
I think its unlikely that JZ is going to be able to survive,, because if what the PP says is true then it follows that criminal charges must be laid, new criminal charges

Commentary Twenty- Two
And that is exactly the intention of the opposition DA

Mmusi Maimane
Without doubt we will put forward criminal actions and I think the law gives us scope to deal with those who are corrupt. if there’s broader cabinet members who are involved, the resignation of the president by de facto means that the cabinet must also follow

Commentary Twenty three
But resignation says Professor Maluleke is unlikely

Tinyiko
This president does not resign. He never quits. He will have to be carried out of the office. I don’t think we can expect him to utter the words resign in relation to himself

ADD BREAK 11 mins 25

Commentary Twenty- four
This week the ANC said they welcomed the findings of the former public protector Thuli Madonsela

Professor Maluleke
In the short term they need to do three things. One ask Jacob Zuma to step down, two ask JZ to step down and third Ask JZ to step down. With almost blind faith people have voted the ANC again and again-I think there is a lot of hard work to rebuild that trust

Commentary Twenty- Five
Short of time and money, the report lists allegations against SAA, Transnet and Denel, and questionable SABC contracts, all to be investigated at a later date. But it does make findings against Eskom, its board and its CEO Brian Molefe, and they are damning.

Bongani
There was of course speculation not too long ago that if Pravin Gordhan were to go Brian Molefe might become the next finance minister. Speculation I say but is that even possible?

Tinyiko Maluleke
It makes sense though in a wickedly warped kind of way. this report relegates Brian Molefe to the dustbin of history – it almost does. I don’t know how he will survive this. But we have to wait for the Judicial Commission of Enquiry



Commentary Twenty-six
In June, Carte Blanche broke the story of how Eskom gave a prepayment to TEGETA of over half a billion rand – and in so doing enabled the Gupta company to buy Optimum coal. In less than a year the Gupta’s have sold off a portion of Optimum coal holdings and made a profit of R2billion rand.

LINK
Eskom pounded CB for our story but the PP is clear, she says that it appears that the conduct of the Eskom board was solely to the benefit of TEGETA in awarding contracts to them and in doing so funded the purchase of Optimum coal which is in serious violation of the PFMA

Commentary Twenty-seven
Brian Molefe and chairman Ben Ngubane have vigorously defended the Gupta’s in the past

Brian Molefe Parliamentary portfolio meeting 31st August 2016
Molefe
What have they done what laws have they broken, because I just work at Eskom and I need to be told don’t do work with them for these reasons and nobody has given me reasons

Commentary Twenty- eight
The report is clear: Tegeta’s conduct and misrepresentations made to the public with regards to the prepayment, and the actual reason for the prepayment, could amount to fraud. Cellphone evidence also places Molefe in Saxonwold around the time Optimum was being negotiated, but Molefe implied he was visiting a shebeen there. Twitter memes went wild

Bongani
And the influence of the Guptas comes out quite strongly in the PP report?
Kriegler
It wasn’t the Gupta’s they were going to the shebeen, we are told
Bongani
Is there something offensive about the fact that a joke like that can be made
Krigler
It is profoundly offence and it is proudly disturbing in that it manifests the contempt … to make a joke about something shows an astounding lack of judgement

Commentary Twenty- nine
On Thursday Molefe shed a little tear, but at a Friday press conference Eskom firmly rejected the suggestion that Tegeta is favoured or that due process was not followed. Tegeta has always denied any wrong doing.

Tinyiko
Can the ANC withstand this? Can the Zuma administration withstand just the public opinion that will form. I’m not so sure.


Commentary Thirty
But Zuma is fighting back. Yesterday he accused NGO’s and the opposition of using the courts to unseat the ANC. Startling words from a man who has used every legal inroad and defence available, to duck a myriad of criminal charges these past nine years

THE END 16 mins 05

PROMO ONE
South Africans were on the edge of their seats as they watched the unfolding events in court and on the streets, as people assembled to voice their discontent against state capture

PROMO TWO
Can the president survive the explosive Public Protectors report
Tinyiko
This president does not resign. He never quits. He will have to be carried out of the office.

PROMO THREE
The president wasn’t the only casualty of the Public protectors report – CEO of Eskom Brian Molefe and the board have been singled out over the controversial Optimum mine deal with a Gupta company

Justice Johann Kriegler I had thought for a long time perhaps over generously that it could just be incompetence but I have come to the conclusion it was malicious intent Commentary Thirteen So Monday this past week was probably not his finest, as Abrahams did his best to spin an embarrassing about turn and withdrew the charges Abrahams As such I have directed the summons to be withdrawn with immediate effect Commentary Policy and political analyst Professor Tinyiko Maluleke Tinyiko Maluleke Shaun Abrahams should have known that there was no case against Pravin from the beginning. So either he is playing the fool or he doesn’t know. If he doesn’t know its horrifying there is someone like that occupies a position like this Commentary fourteen All week, even in parliament, Abrahams was asked the same question. Why should he keep his job? But Abrahams has dug in for the long haul Up Sound Abrahams Will I resign? Certainly not! Certainly not! LINK By Monday evening the rand had rallied a little, the finance minister was safe and by implication so was the treasury- at least for now. Ahead lay Tuesday – state capture day. 01st November NORTH GAUTENG HIGH COURT EFF Advocate Up Sound What is clear is that there is a desperate attempt to try and prohibit the publication of this report Commentary fifteen The opposition parties, and Vytjie Mentor were determined to fight the suppression of the Public protector’s report by the President and minister Des Van Rooyen. Dunstan Mlambo We would like to take time to consider those applications Gauteng Judge President Dunstan Mlambo led a full bench of the high court Bongani What is the cost of all of this? Justice Kriegler Oh! I would think several million rand only on the state capture case, let alone the Abrahams cases and the Ipid case and yet its not over … Bongani Judge do you support the idea that if people in government bring what may turn out to be frivolous cases then they should pay for the costs in their personal capacity Kriegler Oh yes my support is not all that important, that is the law! LINK Everybody knows a lawyer joke right? yet it was the lawyers that held the line even as the Nelson Mandela foundation warned the wheels were coming off the vehicle, that is our state Commentary sixteen Tuesday drew to a close. The opposition had convinced the court they could oppose the interdict but the report still remained a secret. On Wednesday anticipation hung over the capital city Church drums montage. WEDNESDAY 2nd NOVEMBER 2016 Familiar faces dotted the pews in this people’s assembly, titans of the struggle, here to voice their displeasure at the destruction of the democratic project they nurtured Up sound Itumeleng Mosala I wish Steve Biko was here I wish Sobukwe was here, I wish Mandela was here Commentary seventeen But this wasn’t just a gathering of the political celebrities as Barbara Hogan reminded us Barbara Hogan At this very moment Adrian Lackay fighting a R10 million case. There is Johan van Loggerenburg / vlok Symington, Anwa dramat, Shadrack Sibiya ….people who have lived lives of quiet despair because the state has turned on them with all its might for doing the right thing Commentary eighteen Marika Muller left SARS disillusioned by what she witnessed Marika I couldn’t do my job in an ethical fashion Bongani Why is Save SA so important Marika Muller Its about keeping the wolf from the door, if SARS goes if it is no longer trusted, if treasury falls there is no one to stop the looting How close is the wolf to the door? Marika Its at the door. Its knocking. Its right there! Commentary nineteen WED 2nd November Outside the doors of the high court, the EFF grew impatient. Inside the president’s legal team slugged it out with the advocates for the opposition But then, an unexpected turn of events as news spread fast across the capital Barbara Hogan We have just got word that the president has withdrawn his application Up sound wild crowd The people had spoken. The president had buckled Commentary Twenty Before sunset on Wednesday, Madonsela’s State of Capture report was released. The President it said, had violated the executive ethics code and refused to answer her questions LINK The remedial action ordered in the state capture report is nothing short of inspired because it addresses the president’s constant complaint that he wasn’t given ample opportunity to make representations well now he will have to do so before a commission of enquiry and he won’t be able to select his own judge Commentary Twenty- one But can he survive the damning observations in the report? Karima Brown I think its unlikely that JZ is going to be able to survive,, because if what the PP says is true then it follows that criminal charges must be laid, new criminal charges Commentary Twenty- Two And that is exactly the intention of the opposition DA Mmusi Maimane Without doubt we will put forward criminal actions and I think the law gives us scope to deal with those who are corrupt. if there’s broader cabinet members who are involved, the resignation of the president by de facto means that the cabinet must also follow Commentary Twenty three But resignation says Professor Maluleke is unlikely Tinyiko This president does not resign. He never quits. He will have to be carried out of the office. I don’t think we can expect him to utter the words resign in relation to himself ADD BREAK 11 mins 25 Commentary Twenty- four This week the ANC said they welcomed the findings of the former public protector Thuli Madonsela Professor Maluleke In the short term they need to do three things. One ask Jacob Zuma to step down, two ask JZ to step down and third Ask JZ to step down. With almost blind faith people have voted the ANC again and again-I think there is a lot of hard work to rebuild that trust Commentary Twenty- Five Short of time and money, the report lists allegations against SAA, Transnet and Denel, and questionable SABC contracts, all to be investigated at a later date. But it does make findings against Eskom, its board and its CEO Brian Molefe, and they are damning. Bongani There was of course speculation not too long ago that if Pravin Gordhan were to go Brian Molefe might become the next finance minister. Speculation I say but is that even possible? Tinyiko Maluleke It makes sense though in a wickedly warped kind of way. this report relegates Brian Molefe to the dustbin of history – it almost does. I don’t know how he will survive this. But we have to wait for the Judicial Commission of Enquiry Commentary Twenty-six In June, Carte Blanche broke the story of how Eskom gave a prepayment to TEGETA of over half a billion rand – and in so doing enabled the Gupta company to buy Optimum coal. In less than a year the Gupta’s have sold off a portion of Optimum coal holdings and made a profit of R2billion rand. LINK Eskom pounded CB for our story but the PP is clear, she says that it appears that the conduct of the Eskom board was solely to the benefit of TEGETA in awarding contracts to them and in doing so funded the purchase of Optimum coal which is in serious violation of the PFMA Commentary Twenty-seven Brian Molefe and chairman Ben Ngubane have vigorously defended the Gupta’s in the past Brian Molefe Parliamentary portfolio meeting 31st August 2016 Molefe What have they done what laws have they broken, because I just work at Eskom and I need to be told don’t do work with them for these reasons and nobody has given me reasons Commentary Twenty- eight The report is clear: Tegeta’s conduct and misrepresentations made to the public with regards to the prepayment, and the actual reason for the prepayment, could amount to fraud. Cellphone evidence also places Molefe in Saxonwold around the time Optimum was being negotiated, but Molefe implied he was visiting a shebeen there. Twitter memes went wild Bongani And the influence of the Guptas comes out quite strongly in the PP report? Kriegler It wasn’t the Gupta’s they were going to the shebeen, we are told Bongani Is there something offensive about the fact that a joke like that can be made Krigler It is profoundly offence and it is proudly disturbing in that it manifests the contempt … to make a joke about something shows an astounding lack of judgement Commentary Twenty- nine On Thursday Molefe shed a little tear, but at a Friday press conference Eskom firmly rejected the suggestion that Tegeta is favoured or that due process was not followed. Tegeta has always denied any wrong doing. Tinyiko Can the ANC withstand this? Can the Zuma administration withstand just the public opinion that will form. I’m not so sure. Commentary Thirty But Zuma is fighting back. Yesterday he accused NGO’s and the opposition of using the courts to unseat the ANC. Startling words from a man who has used every legal inroad and defence available, to duck a myriad of criminal charges these past nine years THE END 16 mins 05 PROMO ONE South Africans were on the edge of their seats as they watched the unfolding events in court and on the streets, as people assembled to voice their discontent against state capture PROMO TWO Can the president survive the explosive Public Protectors report Tinyiko This president does not resign. He never quits. He will have to be carried out of the office. metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Another big week in South Africa as the NPA steps down on its charges against the finance minister, and the courts deal a blow to the President
metadata.Summary: A week in November By Tuesday evening it already felt like Friday. The wave that has been building over South Africa’s political landscape, this week became a Tsunami. No one is quite sure where it will end. Will the president who has defied the odds, public sentiment and even calls from within his own party to resign, listen? It seems unlikely, but sentiment may be changing deep within the ANC’s core at the NEC. Who knows what the end of the week may look like.
metadata.Further information: The stakes are high but on Monday and Tuesday, the President and his men who seem hell bent on looting the Treasury and destroying anyone in their path, became substantially weaker. On Wednesday the people – business, labour, civil society, religious groups and political parties came out on the streets to make their voices heard. The SAVE South Africa campaign added impetus to a process that is already under way in the courts. Lawfare was once again the order of the day – On Monday the NPA head Shaun Abrahams announced at an impromptu press conference that he was dropping the charges against finance minister Pravin Gordhan. There had never been a case and Abrahams knew it. The case instigated by SARS boss Tom Moyane had descended into a bizarre episode in a SARS boardroom a week before when it became clear that the NPA was still looking for evidence way after they had made such a public announcement on the finance minister and two SARS commissioners. The Vlock Symington hostage drama in the SARS boardroom was up there with some of the best SA could offer – funny if it wasn’t for the fact that the nations fortunes hinge on what happens next. The calls for Abrahams head came thick and fast. He was called Shaun the sheep, internet memes with egg on his face did the rounds and the Law Society called for his resignation. But Abrahams was having none of it – was he embarrassed – he preferred not to answer the question. Would he resign? certainly not. That his decision had cost the country 50 billion rand and an almost certain downgrade seemed lost on him. Banana Republic we are not said the Business Day – more like an absurd soap opera – with each episode getting more and more bizarre. And that was only Monday. Tuesday was the scene of yet another day of high drama as Des Van Rooyen- the weekend finance minister decided to bring an urgent application to court to stop the release of the public protectors report. That application was accompanied by a second from most of the opposition parties who won the right to be joined as parties in the decision on whether or not the public protectors report on State Capture should be released. If there was any doubt about the new PP approach. Well she had none. To quote Phillip De Wet- niks. Nader. None – She would go whichever way the court decided. Not much fight here By Tuesday evening, a full bench of the high court dismissed Van Rooyens urgent application with costs. A glimmer of light and hope for SA future shone from a high court window. On Wednesday the only real decision will be whether or not the court releases the report or not. The report is final. The president is weaker. Thursday and Friday may yet prove more interesting than we can possibly imagine.
